title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the All-China Women's Federation on Issuing the Opinions on Carrying Out Family Education Guidance Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court and All-China Women's Federation

Notice on Issuing the Opinions on Carrying Out Family Education Guidance Work

Fa Fa [2023] No. 7

To the High People's Courts and Women's Federations of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and the Production and Construction Corps Women's Federation of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

To promote the lawful performance of family education duties by parents or other guardians of minors, protect the lawful rights and interests of minors, prevent minors from committing unlawful or criminal acts, and ensure the healthy growth of minors, in accordance with the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Minors, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion of Family Education, and other laws, and in light of judicial practice, the Supreme People's Court and the All-China Women's Federation have jointly formulated the Opinions on Carrying Out Family Education Guidance Work. They are hereby issued for your earnest implementation in light of actual circumstances. Any problems encountered during implementation shall be promptly reported to the Supreme People's Court and the All-China Women's Federation respectively.

May 29, 2023

Supreme People's Court, All-China Women's Federation

Opinions on Carrying Out Family Education Guidance Work

To promote the lawful performance of family education duties by parents or other guardians of minors, protect the lawful rights and interests of minors, prevent minors from committing unlawful or criminal acts, and ensure the healthy growth of minors, in accordance with the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Minors, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion of Family Education, and other laws, and in light of work practice, these Opinions are formulated.

I. General Requirements

1. When carrying out family education guidance work, the people's court shall adhere to the following principles:

(1) The best interests of the minor. Respect the personal dignity of the minor, adapt to the physical and mental development patterns of the minor, give special and priority protection to the minor, and take the protection of the minor's healthy growth as the fundamental goal;

(2) Foster virtue and nurture people. Guide the parents or other guardians of the minor to lawfully perform their main responsibilities in family education, disseminate correct concepts of family education, cultivate and practice socialist core values, and promote the comprehensive development and healthy growth of the minor;

(3) Support as the main approach, intervention as supplementary. Respect the personal dignity of the parents or other guardians of the minor, focus on guidance and assistance, carry out work patiently, carefully, and step by step, promote family harmony, and avoid intensifying conflicts;

(4) Two-way guidance, combine education with assistance. Pay attention not only to educating and guiding the parents or other guardians of the minor, but also to educating and guiding the minor, and, depending on the circumstances and needs, help resolve the actual difficulties of the minor's family;

(5) Professional guidance, focus on practical results. In light of the specific circumstances of the case, determine the family education guidance plan in a targeted manner, promptly evaluate the effect of the education guidance, and adjust the method and content of the guidance as appropriate, ensuring that good results are achieved.

2. The people's court shall participate in, cooperate with, and support the construction of the family education guidance service system within the scope of its statutory duties. In the process of handling various types of cases involving minors, including criminal, civil, administrative, and enforcement cases, it shall lawfully carry out family education guidance work based on the circumstances and needs.

The Women's Federation shall coordinate social resources, through various channels such as family education guidance institutions, community parent schools, and the construction of civilized families, publicize and disseminate family education knowledge, organize and carry out family education practice activities, and promote the construction of a family education guidance service system covering urban and rural areas.

People's courts and Women's Federations at all levels shall strengthen cooperation and coordination, establish a linkage mechanism, and jointly do a good job in family education guidance work.

II. Circumstances for Guidance

3. In the process of hearing divorce cases, the people's court shall provide family education guidance to both spouses who have minor children.

For cases involving disputes over child support, adoption, guardianship, visitation rights, and cases involving special groups such as left-behind minors and minors in difficult circumstances, the people's court may proactively conduct investigations and assessments regarding guardianship and family education situations, and if necessary, lawfully provide family education guidance.

4. In the process of handling cases, if the people's court discovers any of the following circumstances, it shall, depending on the situation, give a reprimand to the parents or other guardians of the minor and may require them to accept family education guidance:

(1) The parents or other guardians of the minor violate the provisions of Article 16 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Minors and Article 21 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion of Family Education, failing to lawfully perform their guardianship duties;

(2) The parents or other guardians of the minor violate the provisions of Articles 17 and 24 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Minors and Articles 20 and 23 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion of Family Education, infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of the minor;

(3) The minor engages in serious misconduct or commits a criminal act;

(4) Other circumstances where the parents or other guardians of the minor fail to lawfully perform their guardianship duties or infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of the minor.

If the circumstances in items (2), (3), or (4) of the preceding paragraph are met, and the parents or other guardians of the minor refuse to accept family education guidance, or still fail to lawfully perform their guardianship duties after accepting family education guidance, the people's court may issue a family education guidance order in the form of a decision, lawfully ordering them to accept family education guidance.

5. When handling cases involving minors, if the parents or other guardians of the minor proactively request family education guidance for themselves, the people's court shall provide it.

6. If, during the process of carrying out family education guidance service activities, residents' committees, villagers' committees, primary and secondary schools, kindergartens, or other entities apply to the people's court for assistance in conducting legal publicity and education, the people's court shall support them.

III. Requirements for Guidance

7. The people's court shall, in accordance with the provisions of Articles 16 and 17 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion of Family Education, and in light of the specific circumstances of the case, determine the content of family education in a targeted manner, and guide the parents or other guardians of the minor to reasonably use family education methods and techniques.

8. In the process of carrying out family education guidance, the people's court shall, in light of the specific circumstances of the case, provide education on guardianship duties to the parents or other guardians of the minor:

(1) Educate the parents or other guardians of the minor to lawfully perform their guardianship responsibilities, strengthen parent-child companionship, and not engage in acts that harm the minor, such as abandonment, abuse, injury, or discrimination;

(2) If entrusting another person to care for the minor, they shall maintain contact with the entrusted person, the minor, and the minor's school or infant care service institution, regularly understand the minor's learning, living conditions, and psychological state, and fulfill their family education responsibilities well;

(3) If the parents of the minor are living apart or divorced, clearly inform them that during the litigation period, the period of separation, or after divorce, they shall cooperate with each other to jointly fulfill their family education responsibilities, and neither party may refuse or fail to perform their family education responsibilities, nor may they use means such as snatching or hiding the minor child to fight for custody or obstruct the other party from exercising guardianship or visitation rights.

9. In the process of carrying out family education guidance, the people's court shall, in light of the specific circumstances of the case, provide legal education to the minor and his/her parents or other guardians:

(1) Educate the parents or other guardians of the minor to establish a sense of the rule of law and enhance their concept of the rule of law;

(2) Ensure that school-age minors lawfully receive and complete compulsory education;

(3) Educate the minor to abide by laws and discipline, and enhance his/her awareness and ability of self-protection;

(4) If discovering that the minor engages in misconduct, serious misconduct, or commits a criminal act, order his/her parents or other guardians to perform their duties and strengthen discipline, while also focusing on emotional persuasion, and educate the minor to recognize mistakes and actively reform.

10. If the people's court decides to entrust a professional institution to carry out family education guidance, it shall also, in accordance with the provisions of the preceding two articles, itself carry out education on guardianship duties and legal education.

IV. Methods of Guidance

11. The people's court may carry out family education guidance at various stages such as pre-litigation mediation, case trial, and post-judgment follow-up, through various forms including court education, explanation of the law and reasoning, on-site guidance, online guidance, psychological intervention, and issuance of a family education responsibility notification.

Depending on the circumstances and needs, the people's court may carry out family education guidance on its own, entrust a professional institution or professional personnel to carry out family education guidance, or jointly carry out family education guidance with a professional institution or professional personnel.

If entrusting a professional institution or professional personnel to carry out family education guidance, the people's court shall track and evaluate the effect of the family education guidance.

12. For situations requiring specialized and personalized family education guidance, the people's court may, based on the guardianship status and actual needs of the minor, notify the Women's Federation in writing to carry out or assist in carrying out family education guidance work.

The Women's Federation shall strengthen cooperation with the people's court, coordinate and leverage the roles of family education guidance institutions, parent schools, women's and children's activity centers, women's and children's homes, and other platforms, and support and cooperate with the people's court in doing a good job in family education guidance work.

13. If ordering the parents or other guardians of the minor to accept family education guidance, the family education guidance order shall state the reasons for the order and the time, place, and frequency for accepting family education guidance.

The frequency of carrying out family education guidance shall be commensurate with the degree of incorrect performance of family education responsibilities by the parents or other guardians of the minor and the degree of the minor's misconduct or criminal behavior.

14. When serving the family education guidance order to the parents or other guardians of the minor, the people's court shall patiently and carefully explain the law, inform them of the important significance of family education guidance for protecting the healthy growth of the minor, and urge them to voluntarily accept and actively cooperate with the family education guidance.

15. If the parents or other guardians of the minor are dissatisfied with the family education guidance order, they may apply to the people's court that made the decision for one reconsideration within five days from the date of receipt of the decision. During the reconsideration period, the execution of the family education guidance order shall not be suspended.

16. When carrying out family education guidance work, the people's court and the Women's Federation shall lawfully protect the privacy and personal information of the minor and his/her parents or other guardians. If carrying out family education guidance through the purchase of social services, they shall require the relevant institutions, organizations, and personnel to sign a confidentiality commitment.

Family education guidance orders issued by the people's court shall not be published on the internet.

17. If a minor suffers from sexual assault, abuse, trafficking, or violent injury, the people's court and the Women's Federation shall, in the process of carrying out family education guidance, cooperate with relevant departments, people's organizations, and social organizations, and take protective measures such as psychological intervention, legal aid, judicial relief, social assistance, school transfer, and placement as appropriate.

If the minor engages in serious misconduct or commits a criminal act, during the process of carrying out family education guidance, follow-up assistance and education shall be provided to the minor.

V. Safeguard Measures

18. People's courts and Women's Federations at all levels are encouraged to establish family education guidance workstations, set up dedicated venues, and allocate specialized personnel to carry out family education guidance work, either independently or jointly with relevant departments, in light of local realities.

People's courts and Women's Federations at all levels are encouraged to explore the formation of specialized family education guidance teams, strengthen professional guidance and professional training, and engage personnel who are familiar with the laws of family education, passionate about the protection of minors, and good at ideological and educational work to participate in family education guidance.

19. In the process of handling cases involving minors, if the people's court discovers that a relevant unit fails to fulfill its protective duties such as education, management, relief, and care for minors, it shall promptly issue a judicial recommendation to the relevant unit.

20. The people's court shall, in light of the characteristics and patterns of cases involving minors, carry out targeted family education publicity and legal publicity and education.

During the National Family Education Publicity Week, people's courts at all levels shall organize and carry out family education publicity and legal publicity and education activities in light of local realities.

21. People's courts and Women's Federations shall strengthen cooperation and coordination with relevant departments, people's organizations, and social organizations, promote the establishment of a linkage mechanism for family education guidance work, promptly study and resolve difficult problems in the field of family education guidance, and continuously improve the effectiveness of family education guidance work.

22. The performance of family education guidance work shall be included in the scope of performance appraisal of the people's court.

23. The people's court shall not charge any fees for carrying out family education guidance work, and the necessary expenses shall be included in the unit's annual budget.

VI. Supplementary Provisions

24. These Opinions shall come into force as of June 1, 2023.
